findings.claim: A memorycard mem_search or mem_context with no project and no cwd or directory now passes the memory gate on the assumption that memorycard's own working directory is the workflow's project. The hook never checks that assumption. If the memorycard MCP server runs from a directory that resolves to a different project (a worktree, a subdirectory, or a server started elsewhere), the read reaches a project other than the workflow's and the gate lets it through. Before this commit such a read was always denied.
evidence: The gate previously denied every memorycard read that named no project (`case read.Project == ""`). The new case `read.Project == "" && ownProject && read.WorkDir == ""` returns an empty GateResult, so it allows the read without comparing anything to `want`.

The justification ("memorycard then reads the project of its own working directory, the session's") appears only in comments at gate.go:547-549 and in the help text. The hook has no code that verifies the server's cwd matches the workflow identity.

MEMORY.md records that mem_* resolves "unknown" from a worktree and needs an explicit project. This workflow uses worktrees under ~/labdrian-sdd-overlay-worktrees, so cwd-based resolution is known to differ from the workflow's project in practice.
The new test in gate_memorycard_test.go only asserts that the read is allowed. It does not cover the case where the server's cwd differs from the bound project.
I did not run any tests or check how memorycard resolves its project, so this is inferred from the diff and the memory note.
